clue.text: Photographing celebrity's heavenly body

parts.note: shooting is taking photographs, as a photographer shoots a scene
a celebrity is a star; the 's links to the definition as 'has'

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps a famous person's beautiful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' sounds like flattery of the celebrity's looks, but it is the astronomical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a meteor, a streak of light in the night sky, loosely counted among celestial objects.

clue.text: Train drivers have been going on these small vehicles

definitions.text: Train drivers have been going on these

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
trikes are three-wheeled vehicles

explanation.surface: A comment on rail workers' repeated walkouts, with small vehicles tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the news: British train drivers staged many walkouts in recent years.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who go on strike stop work in protest; the clue describes those stoppages by train crews.

clue.text: Start working with clique

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a set is a social group or clique

explanation.surface: Someone begins a job alongside an exclusive circle of colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, such as the onset of winter.

clue.text: So tense in this place with enemy restricting resistance

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
here means in this place

indicators.note: the enemy word holds the resistance letter inside, restricting it

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A tense standoff where enemy forces hold back the local resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so are both connectives meaning as a consequence.

clue.text: Lifted school register

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school attendance register has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' poses as theft, and 'register' as a noun; here register is a verb meaning take notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to register it, to observe and take mental account of it.

clue.text: Eccentric lady's nude, dropping attire initially in two shakes

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged
dropping means the chosen letter is removed from the fodder
initially points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman strips off her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping attire initially' removes A from LADYSNUDE; 'Eccentric' rearranges the rest, LDYSNUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: In two shakes is an idiom for very quickly, without warning, as something happens suddenly.

clue.text: Doctor left with little energy after a stroll

indicators.note: the doctor, left and energy pieces follow the A, coming after it

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
E, a small piece of energy, is its physics symbol

explanation.surface: A doctor, low on energy, goes home after a gentle walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, which is what a stroll is.

clue.text: Pretty promising

definitions.meaning: pledging or promising, as one engages to do something

explanation.surface: Praise for someone attractive and full of potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty promising' reads as 'fairly promising'; split it into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging describes charm, and to engage is also to undertake or commit oneself by a pledge.

clue.text: Conservative politician regularly drunk — it's what he wants to do?

definitions.text: it's what he wants to do?

parts.note: Michael Gove is a prominent British Conservative politician

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy Tory MP, and a question about his true ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a long-serving UK Conservative cabinet minister; the definition is the politician's ambition, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Any politician hopes to rule; govern means to hold power and run a country.

clue.text: Esteemed leaders from President Eisenhower's Cabinet entering relaxed

indicators.note: the initials go inside the word for relaxed, entering it

parts.note: rested means relaxed after a break

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Eisenhower's senior cabinet members join a relaxed meeting and earn esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected and esteemed both mean held in high regard by others.

clue.text: Rock star holding good drum

indicators.note: the singer's name holds the letter for good inside it

parts.note: Bono is the lead singer of U2

explanation.surface: A rock singer clutches a fine drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is a small hand drum, usually played in a pair.

clue.text: Youngster's outfit nurse cut short

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing or equipment, an outfit

indicators.note: cut short removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: to tend is to nurse someone

explanation.surface: A child's uniform is clipped by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youngster' looks like a child, but here it is a young cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, so youngster fits in an animal sense.

clue.text: Purchase flat almost with fury

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: level means flat
rage is fury

explanation.surface: Buying an apartment drives someone nearly to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' and 'flat' suggest property buying; purchase here means grip or hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold that gives mechanical advantage, the same idea as leverage.

clue.text: Pries around, grabbing sofa's last spring, perhaps

indicators.note: the turned word grabs the final letter of sofa inside it
around turns the word for pries so it reads backwards

parts.note: noses means pries, as when someone noses about

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word sofa

explanation.surface: A snoop searches the sofa and finds an old spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a coil in the sofa; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is one of the four times of year, an example of a season.

clue.text: Naked, we fancy, assuming adult's excited

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the rearranged letters take in the adult letter
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Nudists get worked up over adult content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges NAKEDWE; 'assuming' places A within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awakened feelings are stirred or aroused, which is what excited means here.

clue.text: Conservative protected by wicked elite — no thing a Labour MP wants?

indicators.note: the Tory letter is shielded inside the rearranged letters, protected by them
wicked suggests something twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory shielded by a corrupt elite, and what a Labour opponent longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges ELITENO; 'protected by' puts C within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labour MP in opposition wants a national vote that could bring their party to power.

clue.text: Chat with carer about odd fellow

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chatting with a care worker about a strange man.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is an eccentric or unusual person, an odd fellow.

clue.text: Tops on French mugs

parts.note: sur is French for on
mugs is slang for faces

explanation.surface: French-style tops printed on mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' suggests drinking cups but is slang for faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfaces are the top or outer layers of things, their tops.

clue.text: Gentle exercises with expert virtually complete

parts.note: PE, physical education, means school exercises
an ace is an expert

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: Mild workouts with an instructor are almost finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful and gentle both describe something calm and free of violence.

clue.text: Worth keeping Meghan, ultimately, Harry?

indicators.note: the word for worth keeps the final letter of Meghan inside it

parts.note: price is the worth of something

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of Meghan

explanation.surface: Is Harry worth keeping Meghan, a royal gossip question.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Harry is married to Meghan Markle; the question mark shows Harry is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry, Duke of Sussex, is a British royal prince, an example of the title.

clue.text: Pester nocturnal animal

definitions.meaning: a burrowing mammal active at night

explanation.surface: Harassing a creature of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Badger is both a verb for harassing and the name of a black-and-white burrowing mammal.

clue.text: Religious education fib? I've no current excuse

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a lie is a fib

indicators.note: no means the current letter is left out

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A pupil's lie about RE homework, with no excuse to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excuse' looks like a noun but is a verb: to excuse from duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty is to excuse them from it.

clue.text: Awful pity if Den misses parking spot

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly done, so the letters are rearranged
misses means the parking letter is left out

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A shame that Den cannot find a parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses parking' removes P; 'Awful' rearranges ITYIFDEN. 'spot' looks like a parking space but means recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot someone is to recognise or pick them out, which is to identify them.

clue.text: Oddly, the male picked up work rate

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word the
in a down entry, picking up a word makes it read upwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A man oddly increases his pace at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or pace of something, its rate.

clue.text: Play golf in the morning and rush, lacking time

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

indicators.note: lacking means the time letter is missing

parts.note: to bolt is to rush off

explanation.surface: An early-morning round of golf, then a hurried dash with no time.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and frolic, to play in a lively way.

clue.text: Obscure book — this could be on the cover

definitions.text: this could be on the cover

parts.note: to blur is to obscure

explanation.surface: An obscure book, and a remark about its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's jacket.

clue.text: Pop group forbidden on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken, signalling a word of the same sound

parts.note: banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: A pop group's song barred from airplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop group is a band of musicians.

clue.text: Best stuff outside Spain

indicators.note: the word for stuff goes outside the Spain letter

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: The finest goods come from beyond Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best stuff' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Best' is the definition and 'stuff' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the best.

clue.text: Warbler's eaten such nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A songbird has eaten nuts of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warbler' suggests a bird; here it is a female singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female nightclub singer, humorously one who warbles.

clue.text: Handsome judge — and intelligent

parts.note: to consider is to judge
able means clever or intelligent

explanation.surface: Praise for a judge who is good-looking and clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handsome' looks like good-looking; here it means large, as in a handsome sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome profit is a large one, so handsome means sizable, considerable.
